text: MixMusic: Spotify and YouTube Music in one desktop player
A free, open-source desktop player for macOS, Windows and Linux: one search, queue and library for Spotify and YouTube Music, with lyrics and podcasts.
MixMusic's home page in the {name} layout and the Mix theme.
MixMusic's home page in the {name} theme and the Blend layout.
One search, one queue and one library across Spotify and YouTube Music, with lyrics, podcasts and downloads, in a free, open-source desktop player you can theme and extend.
MixMusic's window in its default look: the sidebar, a song's cover, up next and the player bar.
A free, open-source desktop player for Spotify and YouTube Music: one search, one queue and one library across both, with synced lyrics, podcasts, downloads, themes and plugins.
Yes, for any purpose. MixMusic is free and open source, under the MIT license or the GNU GPL, version 3, whichever you choose. License tells what each allows, and what else MixMusic includes.

No. YouTube Music's search, home, Explore, artists, albums, playlists, podcasts and radios play with no account, and your liked songs, mixes and history stay on your computer. Sign in to YouTube Music for your own library and recommendations: Accounts tells how.

Only for Spotify. Spotify lets an app serve up to five accounts, and only while its owner has Premium, so you sign in with a Spotify app of your own, made with an account that has Premium. Spotify tracks then play in MixMusic itself, on Windows and macOS, or on Spotify Connect, both with Premium, or from their recording on YouTube Music, which needs no Premium. Spotify walks through it.

Nothing for itself: MixMusic has no account, server, analytics or telemetry of its own. It talks to the services you use: YouTube Music, Spotify and Last.fm, Unison and LRCLIB for the lyrics of the track that plays, and GitHub for updates, yt-dlp and the marketplace. Your library, history and searches stay on your computer. Your data and privacy lists what each feature sends, and where.

In a data folder on your computer, which Settings › About names: %AppData%\MixMusic on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/MixMusic on macOS and ~/.config/MixMusic on Linux. Your sign-ins stay in your system's credential store. Your data and privacy tells what each file holds, and how to move or clear it.
Where does MixMusic keep my data?

The installers, the portable zip, the macOS app and the Linux archive update themselves: MixMusic looks for a new version when it starts and every 6 hours, and asks before it installs one, unless you turn on Install updates without asking in Settings › About. Each update is signed, and one whose signature doesn't match is never installed. The .deb, the .rpm, the AppImage and the Flatpak can't replace their own files, so MixMusic tells you of a new version and downloads its file for you. How MixMusic works tells more.

A .deb for Debian, Ubuntu and their derivatives, an .rpm for Fedora and openSUSE, and for any Linux an AppImage, a Flatpak and a .tar.gz archive whose install.sh installs MixMusic in your home folder, each for x64 and Arm64. The .deb and the .rpm install what MixMusic needs, and the Flatpak brings it along. Getting started tells what the others need.

The macOS app isn't notarized by Apple yet, and the Windows installer isn't signed yet. On macOS, open it once from System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway; on Windows, if SmartScreen warns, choose More info, then Run anyway. MixMusic's code is open on GitHub, and each release lists SHA256SUMS to check the downloads with. Getting started has the rest.
Why do macOS and Windows warn me the first time?

In MixMusic, Settings › About › Report a problem opens a new issue on GitHub in your browser, with your version, system, tools, theme and plugins filled in; nothing goes until you send it. Open logs folder, beside it, shows the log to attach, once you've read it. Or open an issue yourself. Troubleshooting covers the common problems first.

The covers are made for this page. In the app, every track carries the mark of the service it plays from; these songs play from this site, so they have none.
Podcasts, layouts, downloads and lyrics in your language came with the latest release, and more besides. The changelog has all of it.

Turn on translate beside the lyrics and each line shows its translation under it. Japanese can show in romaji, and Korean, Chinese, Russian, Hindi, Thai and other scripts in Latin letters, made on your computer. Lyrics timed word by word light each word as it's sung.
Shows and episodes from YouTube Music and Spotify, in search and in Library › Podcasts. An episode starts where you left it, on another device too, with a speed of its own.
Download songs, albums, playlists, mixes and your liked songs, and they play without the network. Songs added to a downloaded playlist later download on their own.
Blend, the new default, Expressive, Crate and Tiles, MixMusic's look until now. Each sets shapes, density, headings and motion apart from the theme, and every theme shows in every layout.
A track YouTube Music has a 5.1 mix of shows a 5.1 button by the player: six channels on a 5.1 system, mixed down to stereo on headphones.
Send what plays to a Chromecast, a Google Home or Nest speaker, or a TV with Chromecast built in. The queue stays in MixMusic, and the device's own buttons work.

On a MacBook with a notch, the black around the camera widens with the cover and bars that move as it plays. Click it for the player, the progress and the line of lyrics sung now, over any app, full screen too.
From half speed to three times, at the song's own pitch, from the speed button by the player or the command palette.
Keys of your own that play, skip, change the volume or like a song from any app, recorded in Settings › Shortcuts.
The thumbs-down passes over a song from then on, in the queue and in radios. Signed in to YouTube Music, your dislikes go there too. Songs YouTube labels as made with AI can be skipped as well.
YouTube's 24/7 radio channels play live, and music videos can show their picture on the now playing page, muted and in step with the sound.
Every page of MixMusic works across Spotify and YouTube Music. Pick one to see it.
MixMusic's search page for YOASOBI: pivots for songs, videos, albums, artists, playlists and podcasts, and the songs YouTube Music finds, each marked with its service.
One search box for both services

Suggestions come as you type, and the songs, albums, artists, playlists and podcasts of Spotify and YouTube Music land in the same lists, each with a mark of where it comes from. YouTube's videos, such as DJ sets and live recordings, have a list of their own.
YouTube Music needs no account. Spotify joins the same search once you sign in with an app of your own; the guide takes two minutes.
MixMusic's home page: Jump back in, Add Spotify, Liked songs and Your mixes as rounded cards, and Recently played under them.
Tracks of both, in one queue

Play next or add to the queue from any track, album or playlist, then drag to reorder. Shuffle, repeat, crossfade and speed work across both services, a radio carries on when the queue runs out, and the songs you dislike are passed over.

With Premium, Spotify tracks play in MixMusic, one after another without a gap, or on a Spotify Connect device. Without it, MixMusic plays their recording from YouTube Music. A cast button sends what plays to a Chromecast or a Google speaker on your network.
The library's liked songs, with Play, Shuffle and Download, and pivots for mixes, podcasts, downloads and history.
Liked songs, mixes, podcasts and downloads

Like songs from either service and keep them together. Mixes hold tracks of both, and a Spotify or YouTube Music playlist imports into one. Library › Podcasts keeps the shows you follow, and Library › Downloads what plays without the network.
Your history and listening stats, day by day, sit beside them. Playlists of up to 20,000 tracks load in full.
MixMusic's Explore page: new albums and singles, and what's trending, in rows of covers.
Find what you have not heard yet
New albums and singles, the charts of your country, and dozens of moods and genres, each opening its playlists. Under now playing, songs, playlists and artists like what you hear.
Explore comes from YouTube Music, so it needs no account. YouTube's live radio channels play too.
The lyrics panel beside the library, following アイドル line by line, with its Synced, Translate and Romaji switches.

Synced lyrics from Unison, LRCLIB and YouTube Music light up line by line, or word by word where they're timed so, on now playing or beside any page. Translate them, or show Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Russian and many other scripts in Latin letters.
Tune the sound with a 10-band equalizer and its presets, volume levelling and crossfade. Tracks YouTube Music has a 5.1 mix of play in surround on a 5.1 system.
The command palette over the marketplace, listing playback commands and their keys.
Fast at the keyboard, quiet in the background

Every key is yours to change, and global shortcuts of your own work from any app. The tray, media keys, notifications, a mini player and start at login do the everyday work while the window stays closed.
Settings › Accounts, with the four steps to sign in to Spotify.

Sign in to YouTube Music on Google's own page, or import the sign-in of a browser you use, for your home feed and library, and to Spotify with an app of your own. Likes and saves reach the service too.
Last.fm gets every track you hear, and Discord shows what plays on your profile.
Your Spotify tracks and your YouTube Music tracks no longer need two apps. They line up in one queue, in the order you choose.

Each theme is shown in Blend, and each layout in Mix; every theme works in every layout. With Follow the artwork on, as it is at first, the accent takes the colour of the cover playing. More themes, as Neon Nights and Paper Mint, install from the marketplace.

A theme is a folder with a theme.json: eighteen colours, the fonts and a corner radius. MixMusic draws everything with them, in every layout, so a theme keeps working as the app changes. Let it follow your computer, with one theme for light mode and one for dark, or wear the colours pywal or matugen make of your wallpaper.

Plugins are ES modules that add pages, commands, track actions and widgets through a typed API, and install from the marketplace in one click, like a sleep timer or a spectrum on now playing. Every plugin can use the whole API, and MixMusic tells you so before you enable one.
Free for macOS, Windows and Linux. Version 0.5.10; every file is on the GitHub releases page.

MixMusic is open source under the MIT license or the GNU GPL, version 3: one Go program built on MyGo, which draws its windows itself on the GPU, with no browser inside. Fixes, features, themes, plugins and reports of what does not work are all welcome.
